answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to the temperatures at which food can be accepted during receiving:

---

## 🌡️ Food Receiving Temperature Guidelines

### 🥶 Cold TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) Foods
Receive **cold TCS food** (like fish) at **41°F (5°C) or lower**, unless otherwise specified.

### 🔥 Hot Foods
Receive **hot TCS food** at **135°F (57°C) or higher**.

### 🧊 Frozen Foods
**Frozen food** should be **frozen solid** when received.

---

### 🦪 Special Food Categories

| Food Item | Acceptable Receiving Temperature |
|---|---|
| **Live Shellfish** (oysters, mussels, clams, scallops) | Air temp: 45°F (7°C); Internal temp: no greater than 50°F (10°C) |
| **Shucked Shellfish** | 45°F (7°C) or lower |
| **Milk** | 45°F (7°C) or lower |
| **Shell Eggs** | Air temperature of 45°F (7°C) or lower |

Live shellfish should be received at an air temperature of **45°F (7°C)** and an internal temperature no greater than **50°F (10°C)**. Once received, shellfish must be cooled to 41°F. Shucked shellfish should be received at **45°F (7°C) or lower**. Milk should be received at **45°F (7°C) or lower**. Shell eggs should be received at an air temperature of **45°F (7°C) or lower**.

---

### ⚠️ The Temperature Danger Zone
Harmful microorganisms grow well in foods held between **41°F and 135°F**. This temperature range is known as the **Temperature Danger Zone (TDZ)**.

When food sits in the danger zone between 41°F and 135°F, bacteria can **double every 20 minutes**.

---

### ❌ When to Reject Food
Accepting food at unsafe temperatures means starting with a compromised product, no matter how well you handle it afterward. You should **reject any cold items above 41°F** or frozen items showing signs of thawing, and verify hot deliveries arrive at **135°F or above** if applicable.

Frozen foods should **not** have large ice crystals, be discolored, or dried out. Canned goods should have labels, no swelling, flawed seams, rust, or dents. **Never accept home-canned foods** because of the risk of botulism.

---

### 🌡️ Thermometer Use
A **probe thermometer** is a simple tool that can help ensure the quality and safety of the food your restaurant receives by verifying its temperature. Always use a calibrated thermometer rather than relying on touch or visual inspection alone.
